documents.describes: Intended behavior of the raffle contracts (Raffle and RaffleFactory)
NatSpec doc comments in contract sources

requirements.quote: immutable factory
requirements.checkable: RaffleFactory is a direct (non-proxy) deployment whose configuration (implementation, quote token, VRF wrapper, treasury, fee) is immutable/constant with no setter; only append-only registry state changes.

requirements.quote: ERC-1167 clones
requirements.checkable: Each raffle is created by the factory as an ERC-1167 minimal proxy (e.g. Clones.clone of the implementation), not as a full deployment or an upgradeable proxy.

requirements.quote: ERC-1167 clones with immutable implementation
requirements.checkable: The implementation that clones delegate to is fixed (factory raffleImplementation is immutable, set once, with no setter) and has no upgrade or selfdestruct path, so every clone always runs the same code.

requirements.quote: One entry costs 1,000,000 units of canonical six-decimal USDC.
requirements.checkable: The entry price is a fixed constant of exactly 1_000_000 raw quote-token units, not configurable per raffle, and buying n entries collects exactly n * 1_000_000.

requirements.quote: canonical six-decimal USDC
requirements.checkable: The quote token is USDC with exactly 6 decimals (1,000,000 raw units = 1 USDC); the code can enforce the decimals on-chain, but it can only fix canonical token identity at deployment, so that half is only partly checkable in code.

requirements.quote: One purchase mints a transferable ERC721 ticket
requirements.checkable: Every successful purchase (buyEntries) mints exactly one ERC721 ticket regardless of entry count, never one token per entry and never zero tokens.

requirements.quote: a transferable ERC721 ticket
requirements.checkable: Tickets can be moved with the standard ERC721 transfer and approval functions; any _update or transfer hook that blocks or restricts ordinary holder-to-holder transfers is a divergence.

requirements.quote: representing a contiguous inclusive range
requirements.checkable: Each ticket records an inclusive [firstEntry, lastEntry] where lastEntry - firstEntry + 1 equals the entries bought; consecutive tickets' ranges are adjacent and do not overlap (implied: together they partition all sold entries); winner lookup treats both bounds as inclusive.

requirements.quote: Exactly one ERC721 prize
requirements.checkable: Each raffle is bound to exactly one ERC721 (prizeToken, prizeTokenId) that cannot change after creation: no prize-less raffle, no extra prizes, and no ERC20 or ERC1155 prize.

requirements.quote: Exactly one ERC721 prize is escrowed atomically at creation.
requirements.checkable: createRaffle clones, initializes, and pulls the prize into the clone in one transaction, reverting entirely if the escrow fails or cannot be verified, so no raffle is ever active or registered without its prize.

requirements.quote: Reserve met awards NFT
requirements.checkable: In the reserve-met outcome, redeeming the winning ticket delivers the escrowed NFT (and no USDC) to the winner; the doc never defines 'met' (presumably entries sold >= reserve), so the boundary comparison is unspecified.

requirements.quote: Reserve met awards NFT and 95% sponsor
requirements.checkable: In the reserve-met outcome the sponsor is allocated 95% of gross sales (gross minus the 5% protocol fee).

requirements.quote: Reserve met awards NFT and 95% sponsor / 5% treasury
requirements.checkable: In the reserve-met outcome the treasury is allocated 5% (500 bps) of gross sales.

requirements.quote: Reserve missed awards 80% gross to winner
requirements.checkable: In the reserve-missed outcome the winning ticket is allocated 80% (8,000 bps) of gross sales in USDC; the doc does not say where the prize NFT goes in this outcome (presumably back to the sponsor).

requirements.quote: Reserve missed awards 80% gross to winner, 15% sponsor
requirements.checkable: In the reserve-missed outcome the sponsor is allocated 15% of gross sales.

requirements.quote: Reserve missed awards 80% gross to winner, 15% sponsor, 5% treasury
requirements.checkable: In the reserve-missed outcome the treasury is allocated 5% (500 bps) of gross sales.

requirements.quote: Refund outcome pays 100% per entry
requirements.checkable: In the refund outcome each ticket refunds exactly (lastEntry - firstEntry + 1) * 1_000_000 with no protocol fee or other deduction, so total refunds equal gross sales.

requirements.quote: Refund outcome pays 100% per entry and returns prize
requirements.checkable: In the refund outcome the escrowed NFT is returned out of the raffle, never awarded to a ticket holder; the doc does not name the recipient (presumably the sponsor or its recipient).

requirements.quote: Rounding is floor on aggregate protocol fee
requirements.checkable: The protocol fee is computed once on aggregate gross sales as floor(gross * 500 / 10_000): not per entry or per ticket, and never rounded up.

requirements.quote: remainder must be allocated without loss
requirements.checkable: In every outcome the allocations (winner + sponsor + treasury, or total refunds) sum exactly to gross sales, and any rounding remainder goes to a named party (the doc does not say which), so no USDC is stranded in the clone.

requirements.quote: No administrator
requirements.checkable: Neither RaffleFactory nor Raffle has an owner, admin, or role, or any privileged-only function (no pause, rescue, sweep, or privileged setter).

requirements.quote: No administrator, mutable configuration
requirements.checkable: No configuration can change after deployment or initialization: factory parameters are immutable, and each clone's parameters are written once in initialize with no setter and no re-initialization path.

requirements.quote: No administrator, mutable configuration or upgrade.
requirements.checkable: There is no upgrade mechanism anywhere: no UUPS, transparent, or beacon proxy, no implementation-pointer setter, no delegatecall to a mutable target, and no selfdestruct.

requirements.quote: Request window [sale end, end+2days)
requirements.checkable: requestDraw reverts when block.timestamp < endTime and is allowed at block.timestamp == endTime (inclusive lower bound).

requirements.quote: Request window [sale end, end+2days)
requirements.checkable: requestDraw reverts when block.timestamp >= endTime + 2 days (exclusive upper bound) and is allowed at endTime + 2 days - 1.

requirements.quote: Request window [sale end, end+2days)
requirements.checkable: This is implied by the term 'sale end' rather than stated outright: buyEntries rejects purchases at block.timestamp >= endTime, so no entries can be added once a draw request is possible.

requirements.quote: callback accepted strictly before request timestamp+2days
requirements.checkable: fulfillRandomWords records a result only if block.timestamp < requestTimestamp + 2 days (strict); a callback at or after that instant does not resolve the raffle (the doc does not say whether it reverts or is ignored).

requirements.quote: Refunds open at deadline.
requirements.checkable: Refunds open only when block.timestamp >= the applicable deadline (inclusive), through no earlier path (for example a sponsor cancel), never after a result is recorded, and never overlapping the callback window; 'deadline' is undefined in the doc (presumably endTime+2days with no request, or requestTimestamp+2days with an unfulfilled request).

requirements.quote: Callback records result only.
requirements.checkable: fulfillRandomWords only writes the randomness-derived result (winning entry, outcome status, timestamp) to storage: no token or NFT transfers, no external calls, no settlement or payouts.

requirements.quote: Settlement is permissionless
requirements.checkable: settleWinningTicket can be called by any address, with no caller, ownership, or role check.

requirements.quote: Settlement is permissionless, storage-only
requirements.checkable: Settlement makes no asset transfers and no external calls; it only validates the winning ticket and writes the winner, sponsor, and treasury allocations to storage.

requirements.quote: redemption requires current ticket owner
requirements.checkable: Redemption (redeemWinningTicket, and refundTickets if refunds count as redemption) reverts unless msg.sender == ownerOf(ticketId) at call time, so the right follows ticket transfers; the doc does not say whether approved operators qualify.

requirements.quote: burns claim atomically
requirements.checkable: Redemption burns the ticket in the same transaction that delivers the NFT or USDC, so each ticket can be redeemed at most once and there is no separate deferred claim step.

requirements.quote: must revert all effects on delivery failure
requirements.checkable: If delivery of the NFT or USDC to the redeemer fails (revert, false return, or prize not actually received), the whole redemption reverts with burn, status, and liabilities unchanged; there is no try/catch, swallowed low-level-call failure, or fallback credit.

requirements.quote: Sponsor and treasury can claim independently after settlement.
requirements.checkable: The sponsor's USDC claim (releaseSponsorProceeds) succeeds once settlement has allocated the sponsor share, and nothing is claimable before settlement.

requirements.quote: Sponsor and treasury can claim independently after settlement.
requirements.checkable: The treasury's claim (releaseProtocolFees) succeeds once settlement has allocated the protocol fee, and nothing is claimable before settlement.

requirements.quote: Sponsor and treasury can claim independently
requirements.checkable: Neither the sponsor's nor the treasury's claim depends on the other's claim or on the winner's redemption, and a reverting transfer to one party cannot block the other.

requirements.quote: Never move assets between raffle clones.
requirements.checkable: No code path moves USDC or NFTs from one clone to another or pools them (through the factory or with a clone as recipient); each clone's payouts are funded only by its own escrowed prize and sales.

requirements.quote: Quote token and Chainlink wrapper are trusted canonical dependencies
requirements.checkable: The quote token is one canonical address fixed immutably for the factory and every clone, never supplied by a sponsor or caller; the code may assume standard USDC transfer semantics without defensive balance-delta checks.

requirements.quote: Quote token and Chainlink wrapper are trusted canonical dependencies
requirements.checkable: The Chainlink VRF wrapper is one canonical address fixed immutably for the factory and every clone, and randomness callbacks are accepted only from that wrapper and only for the recorded request ID (implied).

requirements.quote: arbitrary prize contracts and ticket recipients are untrusted
requirements.checkable: Sponsor-supplied ERC721 prize contracts are treated as adversarial: calls to them are reentrancy-safe (guards or CEI), escrow and delivery are verified, and a malicious prize contract cannot corrupt USDC accounting, other tickets, or other raffles.

requirements.quote: arbitrary prize contracts and ticket recipients are untrusted
requirements.checkable: Ticket recipients and holders, including contracts with onERC721Received hooks or ones that revert on receipt, cannot reenter to corrupt state or block other users; a hostile recipient can at most fail its own operation.

requirements.quote: Frontend discovery is advisory
requirements.checkable: Too vague to check against the contracts: at most it means factory discovery data (raffleById, isRaffle, RaffleCreated events) is informational and no contract-side decision relies on off-chain discovery being accurate.

requirements.quote: transaction decisions must reread current chain state
requirements.checkable: This addresses frontend code, which is not in packages/contracts/src, so it cannot be checked here; the contract-side analog is that every state-changing function re-validates current status, ownership, and time on-chain.
